title: Global Convergence of Adaptive Sensing for Principal Eigenvector Estimation
claim: Empirical error of our method falls between the proven upper bound and the matching lower bound, confirming the theoretical rate.
layout: 1 log-log plot, three curves, dashed vertical warmup marker, legend bottom-left
description: A single log-log line plot with iterations t (about 10^3 to 2×10^6) on the x-axis and error 1−(ū^T u_t)^2 on the y-axis (10^-5 to 10^0). A red dashed upper-bound curve stays flat at 1 until a vertical gray dashed line marking the end of warmup (t0 ≈ 367k). It then decays toward about 6×10^-2. A blue solid empirical median curve with a light-blue 25–75 percentile band stays near 1, drops sharply around 10^5, and ends near 6×10^-3. A green dotted lower-bound line slopes steadily downward from about 5×10^-3 to 5×10^-6 well below. The legend sits at bottom-left. The title gives d=64, λ1=2, λ2=1. The eye goes first to the blue curve sandwiched between the red and green bounds.
caption: Upper bound (Theorem 4.1), minimax lower bound (Theorem 4.2), and empirical error of Algorithm 1 on shared axes. Empirical curve shows median (solid) and 25–75 percentile band (shaded) over 50 trials. The constant-factor gap between the two bounds is 12 · 864 = 10,368 asymptotically (Section 4); the empirical curve sits neatly between the two bounds. Parameters: d = 64, λ1 = 2, λ2 = 1, step sizes from Theorem 4.1.
abstract: Principal component analysis classically requires full $d$-dimensional samples, yet in various applications hardware limits acquisition to a few scalar measurements per sample. We analyze a compressed variant of Oja's algorithm for estimating the principal eigenvector of the data covariance matrix using only two adaptive measurements per sample. At each iteration, we observe one measurement along the current estimate and one in a random orthogonal direction. We prove that after $t$ iterations, the expected sine-squared error to the true eigenvector is $\mathcal{O}(Î»_1Î»_2 d^2 / (Î^2 t))$, where $d$ is the ambient dimension, $Î»_1, Î»_2$ are the leading eigenvalues, and $Î= Î»_1 - Î»_2$ is the eigengap. We complement this with a matching information-theoretic lower bound of $Î©(Î»_1Î»_2 d^2 / (Î^2 t))$ -- the first for compressed eigenvector estimation -- proving that the $d^2$ factor, an additional factor of $d$ compared to the fully-observed minimax rate $Î(Î»_1Î»_2 d / (Î^2 t))$, is the fundamental cost of compression and cannot be improved. In contrast, any non-adaptive scheme with two measurements per iteration suffers $Î©(Î»_2^2 d^3 / (Î^2 t))$, an additional power of $d$. This separates fully-observed, adaptive-compressed, and non-adaptive-compressed PCA across three powers of $d$. Our analysis handles the noisy setting where the covariance has nonzero trailing eigenvalues, providing the first convergence guarantee for adaptive compressed subspace tracking beyond the noiseless case.
